strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Binds the runtime-selected Product DoD gap into downstream product continuation and journey admission so the scheduled loop can continue from durable Rust-owned evidence.
Requires fresh source decision fingerprints, selected-gap fingerprint validation, explicit continuation/journey authorization, and fail-closed stale evidence checks before task or journey mutation.
Carries bounded selected-gap identity and SHA-256 fingerprints in existing task and journey metadata without exposing raw policy or file content.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with runtime_permission_enforcement and progress_visualization support.
answers.new_capability: Product continuation and product-objective journey admission can prove they originate from a runtime-selected Product DoD gap by carrying selected_remaining_gap provenance and its selection fingerprint through replay-safe task and journey evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M62.1 selected a remaining Product DoD gap, and M61 admitted continuation tasks/journeys, but the downstream provenance still relied on remaining_capability text/hash rather than the selected-gap identity and product evidence decision boundary.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: The loop could select a Product DoD gap but could not require the next autonomous task or journey to prove that it follows that selected gap, leaving Product DoD convergence dependent on caller convention.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M61 admission and M62.1 selection: this phase binds selected-gap provenance into existing admission/replay denial behavior instead of adding another report or selector.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing task.start/headless.continue_once/headless.run.drive continuation and journey surfaces are extended; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The change extends structured provenance and validation, not a summary, digest, history, readiness, inspection, preview, report, or verdict wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime now persists selected_remaining_gap on product continuation/objective provenance, includes it in derived objective identity, and rejects product-objective journey admission when the selected-gap fingerprint is missing, stale, or conflicting.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless caller can advance from product completion evidence to the next task/journey using durable selected-gap provenance instead of authoring or trusting free-form continuation text.
answers.milestone_progress: Moves M62 from selected Product DoD gap annotation to selected-gap-driven continuation authority, likely enabling M62 closeout after review and merge.

exit_criteria: Product continuation provenance includes selected_remaining_gap when the source product completion decision has one
Runtime-derived product objective provenance includes selected_remaining_gap and selected gap fingerprint in derived objective identity
Product-objective journey admission requires expected_selected_remaining_gap_fingerprint for selected-gap-derived continuation tasks
Missing, malformed, stale, or conflicting selected-gap journey source evidence is denied before checkpoint or ledger mutation
No-selected-gap product continuation and journey admission paths remain compatible
No new JSON-RPC method, report, readiness, inspection, digest, history, shell/git/network/service action, provider/tool execution, or workspace mutation is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_selects_remaining_product_dod_gap_and_decides now admits a runtime-derived product continuation from a selected Product DoD gap, asserts selected-gap provenance on task/objective metadata, verifies replay, admits a journey with expected selected-gap fingerprint, and rejects missing selected-gap fingerprint.
Rust unit tests preserve no-selected-gap compatibility for product_objective_continuation_derives_generic_goal_from_remaining_capability and missing remaining capability denial.
VSIX runtimeClient tests accept selected_remaining_gap on ProductContinuationProvenance and reject malformed selected-gap fingerprints.

accepted_capability: Runtime-selected Product DoD gap metadata is carried into product continuation provenance.
Product-objective journey admission validates selected-gap fingerprints before admission and replay.
behavior_evidence: Rust selected-gap continuation/journey behavior test covers success, replay, and missing selected-gap fingerprint denial.
VSIX validator test covers bounded selected gap provenance shape.
safety_boundary: Requires existing explicit product continuation and journey authorization.
Revalidates current product completion decision fingerprints and selected-gap fingerprint before task or journey mutation.
Does not expose raw policy, evidence artifact, prompt, provider, stdout, stderr, command, environment, path, or secret content.
Does not run providers, tools, shell, git, network, services, or workspace mutation.
non_goals: Does not add a new JSON-RPC method or wrapper surface.
Does not create, delete, or mutate workspace files.
Does not add a new selected-gap ranking engine.
Does not auto-plan, auto-run, or auto-merge future phases.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected a selected-gap inspection endpoint because it would not make continuation admission safer.
Rejected caller-authored remaining_capability as sufficient because it lacks selected-gap provenance.
Rejected splitting protocol shape from runtime behavior because this phase needs one vertical slice.
technical_debt: Runtime product-loop logic remains concentrated in crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs.
Selected-gap provenance still follows the bounded policy-declared gap model from M62.1 rather than semantic prioritization.
next_capability_rationale: If this phase merges, M62 should be assessed for closeout because selected Product DoD gaps drive downstream continuation authority end-to-end.
